title: Mild Peruvian-Style Ají Verde
description: Cilantro and roasted mild poblano give this chilled green sauce its color, while cultured dairy and lime give it a clean tang.
equipment: Vitamix or immersion blender with tall heatproof jug

ingredients.name: plain cooked mild poblano pepper
ingredients.note: Mild home-roasted pepper, peeled and seeded.

ingredients.name: no-salt-added low-fat cottage cheese
ingredients.note: Use a no-salt-added product at about 45 mg sodium per 1/2 cup. Low-sodium batch: use 5 1/2 tbsp total.

ingredients.name: plain full-fat mayonnaise
ingredients.note: Use pasteurized mayonnaise at about 90 mg sodium per tablespoon. Low-sodium batch: use 1/2 tbsp total.

steps.title: Smooth the dairy
steps.text: Blend {cot}, {sc} and {may} for 30–45 seconds until the curds disappear.

steps.title: Blend the greens
steps.text: Add {pob}, {cil}, {lj} and {dryga}. Pulse until smooth and vivid green, scraping the jug once.

steps.title: Chill the sauce
steps.text: Transfer to a covered bowl and refrigerate for 20 minutes so the garlic and cilantro can season the dairy.

steps.title: Set the yield
steps.text: Transfer to a measuring cup. Adjust to 1 cup, adding sodium-free water a teaspoon at a time if short. The finished sauce should cling to a spoon.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: Serve cold over warm potatoes or beside tender chicken. Keep the serving bowl chilled until the dish is ready.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 1/2 tbsp plain full-fat mayonnaise in place of 2 tbsp. Use 5 1/2 tbsp no-salt-added low-fat cottage cheese in place of 4 tbsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: No. The chilled emulsion can separate after freezing. Fridge reheat: Serve chilled. Stir well straight from the refrigerator. Freezer reheat: If frozen, thaw overnight in the refrigerator and whisk or blend until smooth. Serve cold. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, omit the lime and use half as much granulated garlic. For dairy-free sauce, use plain unsweetened dairy-free sour cream and unsalted white bean puree for the cottage cheese. Brand changes affect sodium. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 86 kcal, 2.9 g protein, 2.9 g total carbohydrate, 7.2 g fat, 0.3 g fiber, 65 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 55 kcal, 3.6 g protein, 3.1 g total carbohydrate, 3.4 g fat, 0.3 g fiber, 34 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.

equipment: Vitamix or immersion blender with tall heatproof jug

steps.title: Fit the blade
steps.text: Use short pulses in a mini food processor for the mixing step. Scrape down twice. For butter, start softened; for mayonnaise, pulse just until combined.
